gloss.en: advocaat — Dutch thick egg liqueur, the base of a snowball
allesbinder — Dutch instant sauce thickener; cornflour slaked in water does the same job
amandelspijs — Dutch almond filling for pastries such as banketstaaf; like marzipan but softer and less sweet
Amsterdamse uitjes — small onions pickled bright yellow in sweet-sour vinegar; a Dutch borrel classic
andalousesaus — Belgian snack-bar sauce: mayonnaise with tomato and peppers
anijshagel — aniseed-flavoured sugar strands for buttered bread
appelstroop — thick, dark Dutch apple syrup, spread on bread
Aromat — Knorr all-purpose savoury seasoning salt in a shaker
arretjescake — Dutch no-bake chocolate fridge cake with broken biscuits, sold sliced or as a loaf
atjar — Indonesian sweet-and-sour pickled vegetables
babi pangang saus — Dutch-Chinese sweet, tangy tomato and ginger sauce for crispy roast pork
bakgember — candied (crystallised) ginger sold for baking
bakkeljauw — salted dried cod used in Surinamese cooking; soak before use
bamischijf — Dutch snack: a breaded, deep-fried patty of spiced fried noodles
banketstaaf — puff-pastry log filled with almond paste, a Sinterklaas and Christmas treat
basterdsuiker — Dutch fine moist sugar; light soft brown sugar is the closest match
bastognekoek — thick, crunchy caramelised spice biscuit, a sturdier cousin of Biscoff
bavarois — boxed dessert mix sold in Dutch supermarkets for a set fruit or vanilla mousse (like a Bavarian cream), whisked with milk and cream; contains gelatine
bavette — flat pasta between linguine and tagliatelle; linguine works
berenburg — Frisian herbal bitters made with jenever
beschuit — light, round, very crisp Dutch rusk
bitterbal — small round Dutch croquette with a meat ragout filling, the classic snack with drinks
bitterkoekje — chewy Dutch almond macaroon, like a soft amaretto biscuit
blinde vink — Dutch thin veal or pork escalope rolled around seasoned mince
boemboe — Indonesian spice paste (sachet), here for bami goreng (fried noodles)
boemboe — Indonesian spice paste (sachet), here for nasi goreng (fried rice)
boemboe — Indonesian spice paste (Conimex-style sachet), here the peanut-satay one
boemboe — Indonesian spice paste (sachet), here for rendang, the slow-cooked coconut beef curry
bokbier — Dutch seasonal bock beer: dark and malty in autumn, lighter in spring
bokkenpootje — Dutch almond-meringue biscuit sandwiched with buttercream, ends dipped in chocolate
borrelnootjes — peanuts in a crunchy flour coating, served with drinks
borstplaat — Dutch fondant sweets of sugar boiled with cream, eaten at Sinterklaas
boterhamworst — mild, finely ground Dutch slicing sausage for sandwiches
boterkoek — dense, chewy Dutch butter cake, cut into wedges
boterkoekmix — mix for boterkoek, a dense, buttery Dutch cake baked in a round tin; you add butter
brinta — Dutch instant wholewheat breakfast porridge, mixed with (warm) milk
brokkelkaas — rough chunks broken from extra-mature Gouda, sold in tubs
bruine bonensoep — thick Dutch soup of brown beans, usually with bacon
bruine bonen — Dutch brown beans; borlotti or pinto beans are the closest
cassis — Dutch blackcurrant fizzy drink (not the liqueur)
chocoladekruidnoten — marble-sized Sinterklaas spiced biscuits coated in chocolate
chocoladeletter — chocolate initial given around Sinterklaas (5 December)
chocoladevlokken — Dutch chocolate flakes, sprinkled on buttered bread
chocoladezoen — chocolate-coated dome of egg-white foam on a thin wafer base

en: rib of beef on the bone

gloss.en: curryketchup — sweet-spicy curry-flavoured ketchup; what Dutch chip shops call 'curry'
diksap — Dutch thick fruit-juice concentrate you dilute with water, similar to squash
drinkontbijt — Dutch chilled breakfast drink of milk or yoghurt with fruit and cereals
drop — Dutch liquorice sweets, from sweet to very salty
daun salam — Indonesian bay leaf (from the toko); an ordinary bay leaf is the usual stand-in
dubbeldrank — Dutch still drink of fruit juice mixed with water, lighter than juice
eierkoek — light, round Dutch egg sponge cake, eaten plain or with butter
emping — Indonesian slightly bitter crackers made from melinjo nuts
erwtensoep (snert) — thick Dutch split pea soup with smoked sausage
filet americain — Dutch seasoned raw-beef spread, eaten on bread
dried French herb mix (chervil, chives, tarragon, parsley)
frikandel — Dutch skinless, deep-fried minced-meat sausage, a snack-bar classic
frikandelbroodje — Dutch puff-pastry roll baked around a frikandel sausage
fritessaus — Dutch lighter, slightly sweet mayonnaise-style sauce for chips
frituurvet — solid vegetable fat in blocks, melted down in a Dutch deep-fat fryer
Indonesian peanut sauce for gado-gado
gebraden fricandeau — lean Dutch roast pork, sold sliced for sandwiches
gebraden gehakt — Dutch roast meatloaf, sold sliced as a sandwich filling
Dutch spice mix for minced meat (nutmeg, pepper, coriander)
gestampte muisjes — powdered sugared aniseed, sprinkled on buttered rusks or bread
gevulde koek — soft, round Dutch biscuit filled with almond paste
gevulde speculaas — soft speculaas slab with an almond-paste filling
gourmetschotel — Dutch platter of bite-size meats (mini burgers, steaks, sausages) for the tabletop gourmet grill
groene zeep — Dutch soft soap, an all-round cleaner; liquid soft soap is the closest match
groentesoep — Dutch clear vegetable soup, usually with vermicelli and tiny meatballs
hacheekruiden — spice mix (bay, clove, allspice, pepper) for hachee, a Dutch beef-and-onion stew
diced beef for hachee, the Dutch beef-and-onion stew
hagelslag — Dutch chocolate sprinkles, eaten on buttered bread
halvanaise — Dutch half-fat mayonnaise
halvarine — Dutch spread with about half the fat of margarine
hamworst — mild Dutch slicing sausage with pieces of ham
haring — Dutch raw, lightly brined herring (Hollandse nieuwe / maatjes), eaten with chopped onion
thick fresh Chinese egg noodles
hopje — hard coffee-caramel sweet from The Hague
hopjesvla — custard flavoured like Haagse hopjes, Dutch coffee-caramel sweets
hutspotgroente — pre-cut carrot and onion for hutspot, the Dutch potato mash
huzarensalade — Dutch salad of potato, diced meat, pickles and mayonnaise
jenever — Dutch juniper spirit, the ancestor of gin
jodenkoek — large, thin, crumbly Dutch shortbread round
joppiesaus — Dutch snack-bar sauce: mayonnaise with onion and curry spices
kaas — Gouda; mild (jong), mature (belegen) or extra mature (oud)
kaasschnitzel — Dutch vegetarian breaded patty with a melting cheese centre
kaassoufflé — Dutch snack: a breaded, deep-fried pastry pocket filled with melted cheese
kandijsuiker — Dutch/Belgian caramelised sugar crystals used in baking and speculaas; demerara is the closest match
kapucijners — Dutch tinned marrowfat (grey) peas
katenspek — Dutch cooked and smoked pork belly, sliced thin for bread
kemiri — candlenuts, ground into Indonesian spice pastes to thicken them; macadamias are the usual stand-in
kerstkransje — ring-shaped butter biscuit topped with flaked almonds, hung in the Christmas tree
Indonesian salty soy sauce; light soy sauce works too
Indonesian sweet soy sauce
kibbeling — Dutch bite-size chunks of battered, deep-fried white fish (usually cod)
kinderchampagne — alcohol-free sparkling fruit drink in a champagne-style bottle, for children's parties
kipcorn — Dutch snack: a minced-chicken stick in a crunchy cornflake crumb, deep-fried
kipkarbonade — bone-in chicken thigh cutlet
klapstuk — Dutch braising cut from the beef ribs (short rib), for slow stews
kletskop — wafer-thin, crunchy Dutch caramel and nut biscuit
koffiebroodje — Dutch Danish-style pastry swirl with custard and raisins
koffiemelk — Dutch evaporated milk, poured into coffee instead of fresh milk
kokosbrood — firm, sweet Dutch coconut slab, sliced thin and eaten on buttered bread
komijn / djinten — ground cumin (djinten is the Indonesian toko name)
komijnekaas — Dutch semi-hard cheese with cumin seeds (Leiden cheese)
komkommersalade — Dutch sweet-sour cucumber in a creamy dressing, sold as a sandwich spread
krakeling — crisp, sugar-glazed puff-pastry biscuit shaped like a figure of eight
Indonesian side dishes: prawn crackers, atjar (sweet-sour pickled vegetables) and seroendeng (spiced fried coconut)
kroket — Dutch deep-fried breadcrumbed roll with a beef or veal ragout filling
kruidenbouillon — Dutch vegetable-and-herb stock cube
Dutch hard cheese with garlic and herbs
kruidnoten — marble-sized crunchy spiced biscuits eaten around Sinterklaas
kruidnotenmix — mix for kruidnoten, small crunchy spiced Dutch biscuits eaten around Sinterklaas; you add butter
kwarktaartmix — Dutch mix for a no-bake quark cheesecake; usually contains gelatine
laos — galangal, dried and ground (fresh slices at Asian shops)
lasagnemix — Dutch sachet of seasoning and thickener for lasagne sauce
lekkerbekje — Dutch battered, deep-fried white fish fillet (whiting or cod)
leverworst — firm Dutch liver sausage, sliced for bread (the spreadable kind is smeerleverworst)
macaronimix — Dutch sachet of tomato seasoning and thickener for macaroni with mince
Madame Jeanette — very hot Surinamese chilli; a Scotch bonnet is the closest match
Maggi — dark liquid savoury seasoning, used by the drop
maisbrood — Dutch yellow loaf made with wheat and maize flour
Surinamese-style curry powder (blend of turmeric, coriander, cumin)
very young, mild Dutch cheese (May cheese) — a young Gouda works
mergpijpje — sponge log with buttercream, wrapped in marzipan, ends dipped in chocolate
metworst — Dutch dry-cured pork sausage, like a coarse salami
mihoen — thin rice vermicelli noodles (Indonesian bihun)
Dutch brand of full-fat cream cheese; Philadelphia is the nearest match
moorkop — large choux bun filled with whipped cream and topped with chocolate
muisjes — sugared aniseed sprinkles, traditionally eaten on rusks to celebrate a new baby
nagelkaas — Frisian cheese spiced with cloves and cumin
nasigroente — Dutch pre-cut vegetable mix (cabbage, leek, carrot) for fried rice or noodles

nl: boter en olie om in te bakken

gloss.en: oliebollenmix — batter mix for oliebollen, the deep-fried Dutch New Year doughnuts
Dutch spiced breakfast cake — a soft, dark gingerbread-style loaf
ossenworst — Amsterdam raw cured beef sausage, eaten in slices with mustard
pannenkoek — large, thin Dutch pancake; ready-made ones are sold by the pack
pekelvlees — Dutch brined, cooked beef, sliced thin for bread
poffertjesmix — batter mix for poffertjes, small fluffy Dutch pancakes
postelein — mild winter salad leaf, often stirred raw through Dutch potato stamppot
procureur — Dutch boneless pork shoulder (neck end), for slow stews and pulled pork
pudding — Dutch chilled set dessert, much like blancmange
raapstelen — young turnip greens, a classic leaf for Dutch stamppot
ragout — Dutch creamy chicken (or veal) stew from a tin, spooned into vol-au-vent cases
rauwkost — ready-cut raw vegetables (grated carrot, cabbage, celeriac) eaten as a side salad
riblap — Dutch braising steak from the thin rib, for slow stews
roggebrood — dense, dark Dutch rye bread, sold in thin slices
Dutch smoked processed cheese, sold as a sausage-shaped log
wafer-thin Dutch smoked beef — bresaola is the closest match
Dutch smoked sausage (rookworst) — a smoked pork ring or Polish kielbasa works
roze koek — flat, soft Dutch cake topped with pink fondant icing
sambal badjak — Indonesian fried chilli paste, sweeter and milder than sambal oelek
sambal manis — sweet, mild Indonesian chilli paste
sambal oelek — Indonesian crushed chilli paste
sandwich — Dutch soft, slightly sweet finger roll (not a filled sandwich)
santen — Indonesian coconut cream, sold as a block or a carton
saucijs — thin fresh Dutch pork sausage for pan-frying; chipolatas are similar
schoonmaakazijn — cheap Dutch vinegar sold for cleaning only, not for food; white vinegar does the same
seroendeng — Indonesian topping of spiced fried coconut, often with peanuts
sinas — Dutch orange fizzy drink, like Fanta or Tango
slagroomversteviger — powder that keeps whipped cream stiff (like Dr. Oetker Whip It)
slasaus — Dutch tangy, pourable salad cream
slavink — Dutch roll of seasoned minced pork wrapped in streaky bacon, pan-fried
soepgroenten — Dutch pre-cut soup vegetable mix (leek, carrot, celeriac, cauliflower)
soepvlees — pieces of beef (often shin) sold for making Dutch clear soup
spaghettimix — Dutch sachet of seasoning and thickener for bolognese sauce
speculaas — crisp Dutch spiced shortcrust biscuit, like a richer Biscoff
speculaaskruiden — Dutch blend of cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and ginger for speculaas biscuits; mixed spice is the closest match
spekkoek — Indonesian-Dutch layered spice cake
sprits — piped Dutch butter biscuit, often half-dipped in chocolate
stoofpeer — small, hard Dutch cooking pear, stewed with red wine and cinnamon until it turns red
stroopwafel — two thin waffle wafers sandwiched with caramel syrup
suikerbrood — Frisian sweet white loaf with lumps of sugar and cinnamon baked in
sukadelappen — Dutch braising beef (feather blade / chuck), for slow stews
taai-taai — chewy aniseed and honey gingerbread, shaped into figures for Sinterklaas
taartgelei — Dutch clear glaze that sets fresh fruit on flans and tarts
tartaar — Dutch lean minced-beef patty, fried like a burger (not served raw)
tarwebrood — light brown Dutch loaf, between white and wholemeal
tompouce — Dutch puff-pastry custard slice with pink (or, on King's Day, orange) icing
trassi — Indonesian fermented shrimp paste (terasi / belacan)
tutti frutti — Dutch mix of dried apricots, prunes, apples and pears, usually stewed
vadouvan — French-Indian curry spice blend with shallot and garlic
vanillesuiker — Dutch vanilla sugar in 8 g sachets; use a little vanilla extract plus sugar instead
ve-tsin — MSG (monosodium glutamate), a savoury flavour enhancer
vieux — Dutch brandy-style spirit; brandy is the nearest match
vla — Dutch pourable custard, sold chilled in cartons
vlaai — Limburg-style open fruit tart on a thin yeasted base
vlammetje — Dutch snack: a small, spicy spring roll filled with minced meat and chilli
vloeibare margarine — Dutch liquid margarine in a squeeze bottle, used for frying
vruchtenhagel — fruit-flavoured Dutch sugar sprinkles for buttered bread
waspeen — slim washed carrots sold in bags in the Netherlands; ordinary carrots will do
winterpeen — large Dutch winter carrot; any big carrot will do
worstenbroodje — soft Dutch (Brabant) bread roll baked around spiced sausage meat
Zaanse mosterd — coarse Dutch mustard from the Zaan region; wholegrain mustard works
zachte tarwe (Ebly) — pre-steamed durum wheat grains; pearl barley or bulgur is the closest match
zalmsnippers — Dutch pack of smoked salmon offcuts
zure bom — a whole large pickled cucumber (Dutch deli jar)
